question: A vendor offers successive discounts of 12% and 15% on an article whose marked price is ₹2,000. He earns a profit of 20% in the transaction. The cost price (rounded off to the nearest integer) of the article is:
solution:
**Given:**

Marked price of the article = ₹2,000

Successive discounts = 12% and 15%

Profit earned = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (C.P) = Selling Price (S.P) / (1 + Profit%)

Selling Price (S.P) after successive discounts = Marked Price × (1 - First Discount%) × (1 - Second Discount%)

**Calculation:**

First discount = 12%

Second discount = 15%

Marked Price = ₹2,000

S.P after first discount = 2,000 × (1 - 12/100)

S.P after first discount = 2,000 × 0.88

S.P after first discount = ₹1,760

S.P after second discount = 1,760 × (1 - 15/100)

S.P after second discount = 1,760 × 0.85

S.P after second discount = ₹1,496

Profit = 20%

C.P = S.P / (1 + Profit%)

C.P = 1,496 / (1 + 20/100)

C.P = 1,496 / 1.20

C.P = ₹1,246.67

Rounded off to nearest integer, C.P = ₹1,247

**The cost price (rounded off to the nearest integer) of the article is ₹1,247.**
